scope: Real Pi and PiSharp RPC startup using a local loopback Git daemon and offline local dependency. Both install the package and dependency lifecycle scripts once, omit the unavailable host peer, expose the declared skill and prompt template, and send identical expanded skill and template content to the provider. A direct Pi DefaultPackageManager update probe advances an unpinned checkout from v1 to v2; native PiSharp store tests cover the matching explicit update behavior.
limitations: The differential uses a loopback daemon, a local file dependency, and a compiled native extension fixture; it does not exercise hosted Git authentication.
Explicit update is tested through Pi's package-manager API and PiSharp's Runtime store API; this task adds no package update CLI command or RPC reload command.
PiSharp extension implementations are native C# assemblies while Pi loads the paired TypeScript extension entry point.
